title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZR (Application of provisions relating to private companies)

content.overview: Section 378ZR provides that limitations, restrictions and provisions of the Companies Act, other than those specified in Chapter XXIA, that apply to a private company apply, as far as may be, to a Producer Company as if it were a private limited company, insofar as they do not conflict with Chapter XXIA.
content.glance: Private-company provisions apply to a Producer Company only so far as section 378ZR permits and they do not conflict with Chapter XXIA.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZR (Application of provisions relating to private companies). The section applies limitations, restrictions and provisions of the Act applicable to a private company to a Producer Company, as far as may be, except for provisions specified in Chapter XXIA and only insofar as they do not conflict with that Chapter. The section is not a blanket rule that every private-company provision applies regardless of the Chapter's text. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: General application
sections.body: Limitations, restrictions and provisions of the Companies Act applicable to a private company apply, as far as may be, to a Producer Company as if it were a private limited company.

sections.heading: Statutory qualifications
sections.body: Section 378ZR excludes provisions specified in Chapter XXIA from this general application and limits application to provisions that are not in conflict with that Chapter.

sections.heading: Application method
sections.body: For a particular provision, identify the private-company rule, check whether Chapter XXIA specifies otherwise, and assess whether applying the rule would conflict with Chapter XXIA before relying on it.

examples.body: When considering whether a Companies Act provision applicable to private companies also applies to a Producer Company, check the section 378ZR qualifications and any relevant Chapter XXIA provision before applying it.

hypotheticals.question: A party relies on a provision that applies to private companies in a dispute involving a Producer Company. How should section 378ZR be applied?
hypotheticals.analysis: Identify the private-company provision, check whether it is among provisions specified in Chapter XXIA, and determine whether applying it conflicts with Chapter XXIA. Only then assess whether it applies as far as may be under section 378ZR.

distinctions.title: General application of private-company provisions and Chapter XXIA override
distinctions.left: Section 378ZR applies private-company provisions as far as may be, subject to the section's qualifications.
distinctions.right: Section 378ZQ states that Chapter XXIA prevails over inconsistent provisions in the Act or other laws or instruments, while non-inconsistent provisions continue to apply.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 378ZR as automatically applying every private-company provision to a Producer Company.
misconceptions.correction: Apply the express qualifications: provisions specified in Chapter XXIA are excluded and conflicting provisions do not apply through this rule.

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring the words 'as far as may be' when applying a private-company provision.
misconceptions.correction: Explain how the particular provision fits the Producer Company and Chapter XXIA context.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a private-company rule overrides a conflicting Chapter XXIA provision.
misconceptions.correction: Check the Chapter XXIA provision and the statutory conflict qualification before applying the general rule.
